First, we want to find the interval for $\theta $ that corresponds to the first petal. Since the curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin, we want to find the values of $\theta $ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
\sqrt{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\theta )=0.
$$

This gives us two solutions for $5\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ):$

$$
5\theta =-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}\,⟹\,\theta =-\frac{\pi }{10},\frac{\pi }{10}
$$

As a result, the first petal is traversed for $-\frac{\pi }{10}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{10}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/caacb78b0f37dcc58d6568a571c99bc569c7eb95aeacf724d5df33e35ba21fa7.png)

Since there are $5$ petals, the total area bounded by the polar curve can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{\text{total}} & =5\cdot {A}_{\text{petal}} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /10}^{\pi /10}{(\sqrt{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\theta ))}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =5\cdot \frac{5}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /10}^{\pi /10}{cos}^{2}⁡(5\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{25}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /10}^{\pi /10}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(10\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{25}{4}{(\theta +\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(10\theta ))|}_{-\pi /10}^{\pi /10} \\  & =\frac{25}{4}[(\frac{\pi }{10}+\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ))-(-\frac{\pi }{10}+\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi ))] \\  & =\frac{25}{4}(\frac{\pi }{10}+\frac{\pi }{10}) \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$
